clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant disorder combining cerebellar ataxia with prominent cognitive decline, psychiatric disturbance and movement disorders, so it is also termed Huntington disease-like 4
Caused by a CAG/CAA repeat expansion in TBP encoding the TATA-box-binding protein, a general transcription factor
The phenotype is broad and can include chorea, dystonia, parkinsonism, spasticity and seizures in addition to ataxia
Progressive dementia and behavioural or psychiatric change are frequently early and disabling
Reduced penetrance occurs in the intermediate repeat range, complicating interpretation and counselling
MRI shows cerebellar atrophy and, in many patients, cerebral and caudate atrophy resembling Huntington disease
Because CAA interruptions accompany the CAG repeat, the expansion is comparatively stable and anticipation is less pronounced than in some SCAs
Management is supportive and symptomatic, targeting the movement disorder, mood and cognition
reference.pathophysiology: SCA17 is caused by an expanded CAG/CAA repeat in TBP, which encodes the TATA-box-binding protein, a central component of the transcription initiation machinery used by all three RNA polymerases. The resulting elongated polyglutamine tract causes the protein to misfold and aggregate into nuclear inclusions, disrupting global transcriptional regulation through a toxic gain-of-function together with impaired normal TBP activity. Widespread neuronal degeneration affects the cerebellum, cerebral cortex and striatum, explaining the overlap with Huntington disease. The mixed CAG/CAA repeat structure confers relative meiotic stability, so anticipation is modest.
additionalDifferentials: Huntington disease and other Huntington disease-like syndromes
Other autosomal dominant spinocerebellar ataxias (SCA1, SCA2, SCA3)
Wilson disease and other treatable movement disorders with cognitive change
Prion disease presenting with ataxia and dementia
additionalInvestigations: Huntington disease (HTT) testing when the clinical picture is Huntington-like and TBP is negative
MRI brain assessing cerebellar, cortical and caudate atrophy
Neuropsychological assessment to characterise cognitive and behavioural decline
Copper studies and other screens to exclude treatable mimics such as Wilson disease
redFlags: Rapidly progressive dementia raising the possibility of prion disease
Severe psychiatric disturbance with risk to self or others requiring urgent care
Marked dysphagia and aspiration risk in advanced disease
An intermediate-range TBP result of uncertain significance that risks misclassification
reference.prognosis: SCA17 is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that typically advances over one to two decades, with combined motor, cognitive and psychiatric decline leading to substantial dependency; larger expansions tend to cause earlier onset and more severe disease.
pitfalls: Testing only for Huntington disease and missing the phenotypically similar SCA17
Interpreting intermediate TBP alleles as definitively pathogenic given reduced penetrance
Overlooking treatable causes of ataxia with dementia such as Wilson disease before genetic testing
Focusing on ataxia while neglecting the often more disabling cognitive and psychiatric features
references: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: Provide symptomatic and multidisciplinary care, as there is no disease-modifying therapy for the TBP repeat expansion
Treat the movement disorder symptomatically, using dopamine-depleting or antidopaminergic agents for chorea and managing dystonia, parkinsonism and spasticity as appropriate
Manage prominent psychiatric and behavioural disturbance with psychotropic medication and psychiatric support
Support progressive cognitive decline with neuropsychological input, cognitive and social care, and carer support
Control seizures with antiepileptic therapy where present, and manage swallowing safety with speech and language therapy and gastrostomy when aspiration risk is high
Monitor progression and provide anticipatory care planning for the substantial dependency that develops
Offer genetic counselling addressing autosomal dominant inheritance and reduced penetrance in the intermediate repeat range, with careful predictive-testing counselling
